source: McEldoon, Durkin & Rittle-Johnson (2013) Is self-explanation worth the time? A comparison to additional practice
finding: Three arms: self-explain, additional practice (time matched), control. Self-explanation beat control. Against time-matched practice the benefit was modest and only on some subscales.
numbers: N=69 children, grades 2-4, mathematical equivalence (3+4+8=_+8). Three random arms. Abstract only; effect sizes not seen.
quote: self-explanation prompts have some small unique learning benefits
limits: Abstract read only; full text paywalled. Short single-session study with children.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 partly closed: against equal-time practice the human gain shrinks to small. For the agent, compare S5 explanation against extra attempts at equal tokens and expect a small edge at best.

source: Matthews & Rittle-Johnson (2009) In pursuit of knowledge: comparing self-explanations, concepts, and procedures as pedagogical tools
finding: Exp 1: conceptual instruction gave better explanations and conceptual knowledge than procedural instruction. Exp 2: self-explanation prompts after conceptual instruction had no effect.
numbers: Exp 1 n=40; Exp 2 n=48; grades 2-5; mathematical equivalence.
quote: No effect was found for self-explanation prompts.
limits: Abstract only. The null is after good conceptual instruction; there may be a ceiling on the prompt benefit.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: if the input is already conceptually clear, a prompt to explain adds nothing. Apply S5 where the step is opaque, not everywhere.

source: Wang, Min, Deng, Shen, Wu, Zettlemoyer & Sun (2023) Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: what matters
finding: Demonstrations with invalid reasoning still keep 80-90 percent of CoT performance. Relevance to the query and correct step order matter far more than validity.
numbers: text-davinci-002. GSM8K answer acc: STD 15.4, CoT 48.5, invalid reasoning 39.5 (81 percent of CoT), no relevance 11.0, no coherence 23.1. Bamboogle answer F1: CoT 45.2, invalid 39.4, no relevance 23.9. Intrinsic recall on GSM8K: CoT 43.9, invalid 39.8.
quote: CoT reasoning is possible even with invalid demonstrations
limits: Few-shot demonstrations in context, not the model explaining its own steps. 800 GSM8K items sampled. 2022-era models.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: content validity of the rationale matters less than being on topic and in order. A wrong-but-plausible explanation arm keeps most of the gain; error-naming is not shown to be special.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: error analysis
finding: Where CoT was right and invalid-reasoning was wrong, errors were spread over calculation, missing step and semantic understanding. Invalid-reasoning models still produced coherent, relevant lines.
numbers: 20 examples each direction per dataset (Table 3); semantic understanding 35 percent vs 25 percent.
limits: Small manual sample of 20 per direction.
agent_relevance: The model copies the shape of explanation, not its truth. An S5 line must be checked externally; its form alone proves nothing.

source: Snell, Lee, Xu & Kumar (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: At fixed compute, sequential self-revision beats parallel sampling on easy questions; parallel sampling or tree search against a process verifier is better on hard ones. Compute-optimal allocation uses about 4x less compute than best-of-N.
numbers: PaLM 2-S* on MATH. Compute-optimal vs best-of-N: about 4x efficiency gain. FLOPs-matched: a small model with test-time compute can beat a 14x larger model on easy and intermediate questions; little benefit on the hardest.
quote: revisions ... may be a more effective use of test-time compute than sampling N independent responses
limits: Revision model was fine-tuned for revising; verifier is a trained PRM. Not a prompt-only explanation test.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 2: the equal-compute choice depends on difficulty. S5 (sequential explain-and-revise) fits easy-to-medium steps; hard ones need parallel samples. A difficulty router is justified.

finding: Beam search against the verifier degrades on easy questions (levels 1-2) and helps on hard ones; the best method switches with difficulty.
numbers: MATH levels 1-5, binned by model pass rate.
agent_relevance: Supports a capability-dependent effect (gap 2): the same extra tokens help or hurt depending on how solvable the item is for the model.

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han & Zhang (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
finding: No prior work shows reliable self-correction from in-context learning alone on general tasks. Self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists, or in tasks with favorable properties such as decomposable responses.
numbers: Survey; no single effect size. Three research questions (RQ1-RQ3) with findings listed in the introduction.
quote: self-correction is effective in tasks where reliable external feedback is available
limits: Survey of published work; conclusions depend on the papers found.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 closed in direction: an external check (tests, verifier, tool) is the condition under which explain-then-revise turns positive.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: Meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models. CoT helps on symbolic, math and logic; on other categories the gain is about 0.7 points.
numbers: Mean CoT gains: symbolic 14.2, math 12.3, logical 6.9. Top three categories 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without. Other categories 56.8 vs 56.1.
quote: a truly fair comparison between the methods should match the compute of the two methods
limits: Zero-shot CoT, not self-explanation of worked steps. Authors note compute is not matched.
agent_relevance: Gaps 9 and 1: stepwise explanation pays on formal multi-step tasks, little elsewhere. Authors say a compute-matched comparison is missing, which is exactly our gap 1.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) planning vs execution
finding: Most of CoT's gain comes from symbolic execution; it underperforms a symbolic solver. On MMLU, CoT is near identical to direct answering unless an equals sign is present.
limits: MMLU split by equals sign is a proxy.
agent_relevance: Where a tool can run the step (code, solver), the tool beats prose explanation; use S5 prose for steps that a tool cannot check.

source: Lightman et al. (2023) Let's Verify Step by Step
finding: Process supervision (step-level labels) beats outcome supervision as a reward model on MATH.
numbers: Best-of-1860: PRM 78.2 percent solved, ORM 72.4, majority voting 69.6. PRM800K: 800K step labels, 75K solutions, 12K problems.
limits: Verifier trained on large human step labels; MATH subset; GPT-4 base.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: step-level judgement beats final-answer judgement on long chains. Supports checking each S5 line, not only the end result.

source: Panickssery, Bowman & Feng (2024) LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
finding: LLM judges recognize their own text and score it higher. Self-preference strength rises linearly with self-recognition, and fine-tuning for recognition raises bias.
numbers: GPT-4 and Llama 2 have non-trivial out-of-box self-recognition; GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 fine-tuned on CNN/DailyMail and XSUM; linear correlation shown in Figure 1.
limits: Summarization tasks; causality shown only by fine-tuning controls.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: an agent grading its own explanations will be biased upward. Grade with a different model or an executable check.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
finding: GPT-4 as judge agrees with humans over 80 percent, the same as human-human agreement, but has position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias and limited reasoning ability.
numbers: Agreement above 80 percent on MT-bench and Arena.
limits: Pairwise preference on chat answers, not correctness of reasoning steps.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: use pairwise or reference-based grading, randomise order, keep explanations short to limit length bias.

source: Tyen, Mansoor, Carbune, Chen & Mak (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: LLMs are poor at finding the step with the mistake, but correct well when told where it is. Poor self-correction comes from poor mistake finding, not from poor fixing.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake; GPT-4 best mistake-finding overall 52.87 with direct step-level prompting; five models tested; 5 reasoning tasks.
quote: LLMs' inability to find logical mistakes
limits: Traces from PaLM 2 on BIG-Bench tasks.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 4: the useful part is correct error location (naming what is wrong). An S5 line helps only if it points at the right step; otherwise it hurts.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) minimum mistake-finding accuracy for backtracking
finding: Simulated classifiers: backtracking is still effective without gold labels, but accuracy losses plateau only at about 65 percent mistake-finding accuracy; trained small classifiers did not reach the needed threshold.
numbers: PaLM 2 Unicorn 3-shot baseline vs trained classifier; gains on 4 of 5 held-out tasks (Table 7).
agent_relevance: Gap 4: an error-finder needs roughly 60-70 percent accuracy before acting on it. Below that, no revision is safer.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: Self-feedback plus refinement improved 7 tasks by about 20 points absolute on average, but math reasoning gained 0 because the model said everything looks good in 94 percent of cases.
numbers: GPT-3.5/GPT-4. Math reasoning 64.1 to 64.1 (0). Sentiment reversal GPT-3.5 8.8 to 30.4. Math gains above 5 points if an external source flags wrong answers.
quote: feedback for 94% instances is 'everything looks good'
limits: Preference tasks are judged by an LLM; compute not matched to resampling.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 4: specific feedback helps; in formal domains self-feedback fails without an external wrongness signal.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine feedback quality ablation
finding: Specific, actionable feedback beats generic feedback, which beats no feedback.
numbers: Sentiment transfer 43.2 (specific) vs 31.2 (generic); Code optimization 27.5 / 26.0 / 24.8 (specific / generic / none).
agent_relevance: Direct support for S5 wording: name the exact problem and the fix direction, not 'check again'.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (cross-link)
finding: Cited in Kamoi and Tyen as the base result; numbers are in evidence_c, not re-opened here.

source: Chi et al. (1989) and Chi et al. (1994) primary texts
finding: Not opened. Wiley returned HTTP 403 and the ASU lab copy redirected to a login. Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv APIs were rate-limited and the search budget was spent, so gap 5 stays open.
agent_relevance: Keep the Chi 1989 and Chi 1994 numbers marked second-hand.

finding: Not opened (ScienceDirect 403). Only the title is known: instructional explanations can reduce self-explanation.
